**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.2. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

An inner product measures alignment. Linear predictors use a dot product to combine the feature vector with parameter weights, and projected representations use it to obtain coordinates.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
\langle\boldsymbol x,\boldsymbol z\rangle=\boldsymbol x^\top\boldsymbol z=\sum_{i=1}^{d}x_iz_i
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

For orders x=(1,1) and z=(2,2), the dot product is 4. For x=(1,0) and z=(0,1), it is zero: these directions are orthogonal in the Euclidean geometry.

## What follows, and what does not

An inner product is not a distance: it can grow merely because the vectors are long. Normalising vectors yields cosine similarity when both are nonzero.

## Test your reasoning

Which two of (1,1), (1,-1), and (2,2) are orthogonal?
